questions: Product and holonomy convention (NOTES l.338): the notes do not say whether hol is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism for concatenation, nor where the cyclic order starts. Reading taken: mathlib's group law on pi_1 ([g]*[d] = [d then g]) and gx's holonomy homomorphism; then hol(C-) = P(p1)...P(pa) holds with p_a, ..., p_1 the order in which the arcs leave the base point counterclockwise from the direction in which C- leaves it (as a concatenation, C- = gamma_{p_a} ... gamma_{p_1}, gamma_{p_a} first).

The sentence 'Lifted to G~, this defines the total angle Theta-' (NOTES l.341-342, with P~(x) the rotation by the real cone angle, l.330-331) is not formalized. Reading taken: Theta- is the angle of the elliptic RP1-circle C- from the hyperbolic side (the notes' second sentence). The session's own reasoning [r], NOT evidence: the canonical lifts do not multiply termwise, since a regular point has P~ = delta (rotation by 2 pi) although its loop is trivial. The session expects hol~(C-) = delta^(1-a) P~(p1)...P~(pa). Its checks are a = 0 (D- = H^2, angle 2 pi), a = 1, and the light-particle limit, where the total deficit is the sum of the deficits. If the notes mean Theta- = angle(P~(p1)...P~(pa)), that is off by 2 pi (a-1).

pi_1(D- minus {p_i}) is free on the gamma_i (NOTES l.339): not formalized, and not used. The statement of (M1) needs only the relation [C-] = prod [gamma_i], which is proved. Should freeness be its own target?

not_stated.claim: Theta- = Theta+ as real numbers (NOTES l.344, 347-349; BBS l.3013)
not_stated.obstruction: Stating it needs objects that no library has at this pin: HS^2 as a (SO0(1,2), HS^2) model with its analytic action, the photon circles C+- of a singular HS-sphere, their RP1-structures from the hyperbolic side, the universal cover G~ of PSL(2,R) acting on RP1~, and the real angle of an elliptic RP1-circle. Proving it also needs the de Sitter geometry of A. A route, the session's own reasoning [r], NOT evidence: lift the developing map of A to the universal cover of the closed de Sitter annulus dS~ union R- union R+; the two boundary lines then carry the same lifted holonomy g~; the left isotropic foliation identifies R- with R+ G~-equivariantly; so the translation numbers of g~ on R-+ agree. This would give Theta- = Theta+ whenever C+- are elliptic and A is regular.

findings: NOTES-3+1.md l.329, l.343-346 against l.214-216, 227-229 (N3) and l.477 (N5). Take one orientation for every loop: P(x) the holonomy of a small loop positive for Sigma's orientation (l.329), and C+- the positive boundaries of D+- ('the proof is the same', l.343). Then (M1)+(M2)+(M3) give P(p1)...P(pa) = P(q1)...P(qb). But on the oriented sphere the annulus runs the positive boundary of D+ backwards, so hol(C-) hol(C+) = 1. This is N3's own relation 'prod P_i = 1' (l.215, 229) and the 'P_in^-1' of N5 (l.477). In that reading (M3) holds iff hol(C-)^2 = 1. Lean: GX.SphereData.holIn_mul_holOut, GX.SphereData.sphere_relation, GX.SphereData.holIn_eq_holOut_iff, all proved. Counterexample GX.m3_printed_fails, proved: on the Riemann sphere, with the incoming particle at 0, the outgoing one at infinity, D- = {|z| <= 1}, A = {1 <= |z| <= 2} and D+ = {|z| >= 2} plus infinity, both boundaries are positive (winding +1 around 0 in the chart z, +1 around infinity in the chart 1/z). For every holonomy rho_g = g^wind with g^2 != 1, rho_g(C-) = g != g^-1 = rho_g(C+). [r], not formalized: the link of a point on a massive particle line (a = b = 1) has holonomy of this form with g the rotation by the deficit, so it violates the positive-positive reading unless the cone angle is pi. Corrected form, proved (GX.InteractionData.holIn_eq_holOut): (M2)-(M3) hold when C+ and the loops around the q_j are oriented as C- transported across A, which is negative for Sigma. In Sigma-positive terms, (M2)+(M3) read hol(C-) = P(qb)^-1 ... P(q1)^-1. One of the two conventions has to be fixed in the notes.

kb_proposals: mathlib's FundamentalGroup is End in the fundamental groupoid: fromPath [p] * fromPath [q] = fromPath [q.trans p] (the right factor runs first); say so whenever an ordered product of loops is stated.

Relations among polygonal loops in a subspace S of R^2 need no homotopy: build the edges with GX.segIn from convex boxes inside S, then close the identity in Path.Homotopic.Quotient with simp only [mk_trans, mk_symm, trans_assoc] plus a cancellation lemma p.symm.trans (p.trans q) = q. Straight lines in convex boxes (GX.homotopic_of_convex_subset) supply the remaining homotopies.
In an induction over the vertices of a model, clamp the indices (height min k a) so that every edge exists for every k; this avoids dependent membership proofs.
If a base point is a def equal to a vertex, simp's mk_trans fails silently: the endpoints do not unify at reducible transparency. Make the base point an abbrev.

I x I is simply connected: haveI : ContractibleSpace I := (convex_Icc 0 1).contractibleSpace _, then the product instance and SimplyConnectedSpace.ofContractible; SimplyConnectedSpace.paths_homotopic then gives the annulus lemma GX.mk_eq_conj_of_annulus.

gx has a winding number for loops of C minus 0 (GX.cWinding in GX.Branched.Paths); GX.windingHom packages it as a homomorphism pi_1 -> Multiplicative Z, and composing with zpowersHom gives holonomies g^wind for counterexamples.
